verses.1: Al-Mizan, invoking al-Rāghib, gives īlāf or li-īlāf as creating harmony, affinity, and here peace and security for Quraysh, the Prophet’s clan descended from al-Naḍr b. Kanānah. Riḥlah, according to Majmaʿ al-bayān, is journeying on a strong camel; here it denotes their necessary winter trade journey to Yemen and summer journey to the Levant, since Mecca could not support agriculture or livestock. The Sacred House’s honor protected them from highwaymen on the road and raids at home. The lām signifies taʿlīl: God is the subject who created this security and made the journeys safe and smooth.
verses.2: Al-Mizan, invoking al-Rāghib, gives īlāf or li-īlāf as creating harmony, affinity, and here peace and security for Quraysh, the Prophet’s clan descended from al-Naḍr b. Kanānah. Riḥlah, according to Majmaʿ al-bayān, is journeying on a strong camel; here it denotes their necessary winter trade journey to Yemen and summer journey to the Levant, since Mecca could not support agriculture or livestock. The Sacred House’s honor protected them from highwaymen on the road and raids at home. The lām signifies taʿlīl: God is the subject who created this security and made the journeys safe and smooth.
verses.3: Al-Mizan takes the fāʾ in fal-yaʿbudū either conditionally: if Quraysh do not serve God for His countless other favors, they must serve the Lord of this House because He facilitated their two journeys; or as tafṣīl, requiring worship without distinguishing circumstances, like fa-iṣbir (74:7). On the chapter’s independent theme, verses 106:1-3 therefore command worship because God’s security gave Quraysh a secure livelihood. Those who make this sūrah a continuation of al-Fīl instead take lām in li-īlāf as justification of something elided: the destruction of the Riders was an added blessing to their journeys—al-Farrāʾ is reported to read lām as ilá—or it secured Quraysh in Mecca, or enabled their return after Abrahah so that Muḥammad could be born and later appointed as a bearer of glad tidings and warnings. Al-Mizan says the issue is whether the chapter’s theme and context support these readings.
verses.4: Al-Mizan identifies food and security as the two evident divine favors flowing from Quraysh’s journeys: they were sustained in infertile country and safe while their neighbours were not. These favors command their worship of the Lord of this House, who managed their affairs in the best way.
